gen-syne-gf-geist-mono: Loud, smooth and a bit strange, Syne heads the page with curves that never pinch. Geist Mono follows in fixed-width code letters with generous side gaps, so a long paragraph ticks along like a typewriter.
gen-syne-gf-major-mono-display: Major Mono Display reads like neon glass, its tube-like monospace strokes sweeping open with plenty of space around each letter. Syne stands over it with a plain, confident line, and a long paragraph would feel deliberate, almost lit from within.
gen-syne-gf-martian-mono: Syne leads with an experimental, commanding line, smooth curves and lowercase that climbs nearly to the capitals. Martian Mono does the opposite job, spacing its fixed-width letters loosely so each word breathes.
gen-syne-gf-spline-sans-mono: Spline Sans Mono sets fixed-width letters with lowercase nearly matching the capitals, all in one bold, uniform stroke. Syne sits above it with a similar plain stripe of ink, so the two feel cut from one stencil.
gen-syne-gf-victor-mono: Syne brings an experimental, commanding voice, with smooth curves and lowercase that rises close to the capitals. Yet Victor Mono is the surprise, its monospace bowls left open on one side and its spacing loose, which gives the pair a precise but restless charm.
gen-syne-newsreader: Commanding, a little odd, Syne draws its horizontals as heavy as its verticals and lifts its lowercase high. Newsreader follows with a restrained serif stroke and open curves, so a long article would read with quiet authority.
gen-tourney-fs-chillax: Chunky, stretched and sporty, Tourney shouts in one cut width with oversized small letters. And Chillax loosens up below it with spaghetti-like lines, so give that sans a little more size than you'd expect.
gen-tourney-fs-plein: Tourney stamps out wide-tracked words in one fixed width, bulky lowercase included. Plein settles beneath it as a reliable, clean sans, with a clear channel leading into each round letter.
gen-tourney-fs-spline-sans: Stretched, wide-tracked words in a single cut width make Tourney instantly athletic. Spline Sans then reads as a friendly plain sans, with open gaps where curves meet stems, so a long page stays approachable.
gen-tourney-fs-synonym: Wide, stretched and built like a scoreboard, Tourney hits hard with every stroke cut to one width. Synonym does the quieter work, laying down a dependable sans line with open curves for text that needs to be read.
